answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small time-locked stake before it may harvest rewards, much like a bee must work a mesa flower before tasting its nectar. The stake is slashed if the agent's attestations contradict the consensus, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive: each clone risks losing its own deposit. Honest agents meanwhile accumulate a transparent reputation record, a crystal-clear history peers can verify before trusting a newcomer with paid work.
